audit: Did You Know That? No. 01 - Time, Compressed - independent read-only audit v4
master: dyk-01-time-compressed-1080P.mp4 (ffprobe: 1920x1080, 30/1 fps, video 574.400 s, audio 574.433 s)
method: Viewed all 48 sweep sheets (sweep-v3, 1 frame/s, 0:00-9:33) against timeline-by-second.txt; absolute word times computed from narration/*.words.json + timeline.json shot offsets (shot order from build_final.py); facts checked against RESEARCH.md F1-F26; suspect tiles re-checked in full 480x270 sweep frames (sweep-v3/frames).

verifiedFixes.evidence: TcPromise chip builds in three steps: 1:10 'IN EACH ONE' only, 1:11 '+ you wake up as', 1:12 '+ someone else' (gold), matching 'In each one' 1:10 / 'you will wake up as someone' 1:11 / 'else' 1:12; ui-click at 1:10.

1500 Day Clock legend builds 1:33 (1 row) -> 1:34 (3 rows) -> 1:35 (all 7 rows) with ui-clicks 1:33-1:35. Highlight moves: 'First sleep' bold at 1:36 (word 1:36.06), 'Second sleep' bold 1:37-1:38 (word 1:37.02), 'Awake in the dark - pray, talk, visit' bold and ring segment lifted 1:39-1:41 (word 'prayed' 1:39.25).
5:45-5:50 'One lifetime now holds more change than whole centuries / once did.' wraps to two centred lines spanning roughly x=190-1730 px of 1920 (inside the 90% title-safe box, clear of the HUD).

Frame f0366 (6:05): phone shows 4 coloured notification rows and a red '12' badge; 6:04 phone empty and glowing; pop-reveals at 6:04/6:05 ('already' 6:04.81, 'checked' 6:05.19). Caveat: replaced by the DYK card at about 6:06.0, so the notifications are on screen for only about 1.2 s (see LOW L3).

findings.issue: The coffee reveal is shown before it is spoken. The narration builds to a reveal ('The air smells of smoke, and of something new. Coffee.'), but the era title subtitle says 'London - the smell of coffee' from 2:19, and a steaming coffee cup ('LONDON - 1652 - SOMETHING NEW IN THE AIR') appears at 2:23. Both come before the word 'Coffee.' (2:26.46-2:27.10). The cup also appears with no SFX, and the word 'Coffee.' gets no visual or sound beat of its own.
findings.evidence: Sheets 11-12: 2:19-2:22 title card with subtitle 'London - the smell of coffee'; 2:23-2:26 cup on screen; timeline-by-second shows no SFX at 2:23 or 2:26; words.json puts 'Coffee.' at 2:26.46 absolute.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the subtitle to something like 'London - something new in the air'. Bring in the cup on 'Coffee.' (2:26.5) with a pop or warm-shimmer, or show a silhouette or '?' cup until then.

findings.issue: The era subtitle 'England - a village - midnight' shows about 2 s before the narration's 'It is midnight.' (1:25). It is the same scene-setting pre-empt as V4-M1, but milder because nothing here is staged as a reveal.
findings.evidence: Sheet 06 tile 1:23 and sheet 07 tiles 1:24-1:28; timeline 1:25 'It is midnight.'
findings.suggestedFix: Optional: subtitle 'England - a village - night', or leave as is.

findings.issue: The 'LIVING LONGER THAN EVER' chip lasts only about 1.5 s. It appears on 'living' (7:40.47), then at about 7:42.0 the whole UN card is swapped for the Goldman Sachs card, which leaves very little time to read it.
findings.evidence: Sheet 38: chip visible only in the 7:41 tile; 7:42 tile already shows the Goldman card fading in ('Goldman' spoken 7:42.36).
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the UN card plus chip until 'Goldman' (7:42.3), or stack the Goldman card below the UN card instead of replacing it.

findings.issue: The phone notifications and red 12 badge (the V2-M4 fix) are on screen for only about 1.2 s before the DYK card covers them. They are visible, but close to a flash.
findings.evidence: Sheet 30: 6:04 empty phone, 6:05 notifications + '12', 6:06 DYK card only. 'Did' spoken at 6:06.37. Sub-second duration not measured (ffmpeg stills held, see notVerified).
findings.suggestedFix: Land the notifications on 'already' (6:04.8) and delay the DYK card to 'Did' (6:06.37), or slide the phone aside instead of covering it.

findings.issue: Long static holds while narration continues: the TIME SAVED arrow alone (about 4 s), the newspaper alone (about 5 s), the Ford DYK card (about 8 s) and the outro century card (about 5 s). Each is backed by narration, so none is empty, but the picture goes still.
findings.evidence: Sheets 01, 13, 26-27, 43: identical consecutive tiles across these ranges.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a slow push-in or drift, or a secondary build (for example highlight '$5' on 'five dollars' and 'eight hours' on 'eight').

findings.issue: The knock-solid SFX (0.34) on 'heard noon twice' has no visible new event at 1 fps: the 4:15 and 4:17 tiles are identical. It may be a sub-second pulse the sweep cannot see.
findings.suggestedFix: Pulse both clocks (or flash a '2x' tag) on the knock, or drop the cue.

findings.issue: On-screen 'Fifteen times faster.' is a derived claim that is never narrated. 10 days / 16 h = 15x, which matches F7 as narrated. With PBS's 16.5 h it would be about 14.5x, so '15x' is a rounding.
findings.evidence: Sheet 23 tiles 4:44-4:46; RESEARCH.md F7 (about 16 h; PBS 16.5 h; about 10 days by steamer).
findings.suggestedFix: Optional: change to 'About fifteen times faster.' or note the derivation in RESEARCH.md.

checkedClean: No CRITICAL fact errors: every on-screen number/year matches RESEARCH.md (0.1 s F14, weeks F26, about 35 F2, 1605 Strasbourg F3, 1656 and about 15 min to about 15 s F4, HMS Deptford Nov 1761-Jan 1762 and about 5 s F6, 1858 16 h vs 10 days F7, 18 Nov 1883 F8, 1881 Beard F9, 12 h 30 min to 93 min F10, 1903/1969 F11, 1930 15 h F12, 3,000+ / 1,354 Germany 2017 F13, 10.2 bn / peak 10.3 bn mid-2080s F16, Factory Act 1850 2 pm F21, $5 / 8 h / 1926 F22, 6 h 38 min F23, 300 million exposed F24, 56 of 61 F25).
Brand is consistent: 'Did You Know That?' logo and HUD, Dexty.live (HUD, outro pill, end screen footer); the end screen handle is @Did-You-Know-that-2026. No foreign brands.

Reveal timing: rechecked against absolute word times, all other reveals land on or within about 0.5 s of their word (e.g. Science 0:41.80 -> card 0:42; time discipline 3:35.95 -> 3:36; telegraph 4:54.20; reveal chips 7:14.66-7:19.74 each in the following tile).
No dips to black or empty frames seen at 1 fps. The dark tiles at 0:25, 0:29, 1:02, 3:08, 6:44, 7:27, 8:29 and 9:19 are intentional transition builds with whoosh/impact cues.

Text sits inside title-safe with no overlaps. The HUD stays on the bottom band. Note: the sweep SHEETS crop about 8 px off the top of each tile, so the top-left era tag looks clipped there; the full sweep frames (f0101, f0366, f0381) show it is complete. This is an artifact of the sheet montage, not a video bug.

End screen: begins about 9:19.4 (ES_F computed from build_final.py + durations.json = 559.37 s) and runs to 574.43 s = about 15.07 s. Layout: COMMENT OF THE WEEK (marked EXAMPLE), No. 02 THE SUN, SUBSCRIBE, Dexty.live footer.
notVerified: Sub-second checks (exact reveal frames, flash durations, sub-second black dips): danslab-workflow check HELD both a still-extraction command and a write-nothing blackdetect pass (14.15 GiB free vs 46.04 GiB reserve). Per instructions, no ffmpeg was run.
Audio by ear (loudness, ducking, SFX level and timbre, voice identity). SFX were checked only against the timeline cue list.
Fine 1080p text (tiny source lines) was read at 480x270, so typos in micro-text cannot be ruled out.
